content_preview.title: Transmission BitTorrent Client Forks Into ReTransmission Over Dispute on Adding More Maintainers
content_preview.summary: Transmission's maintainers have split the widely used BitTorrent client into a new project, ReTransmission, after a long-running disagreement over whether to add more maintainers.
content_preview.body_excerpt:
## Overview

Transmission, one of the best-known open-source BitTorrent clients on Linux, has been forked into a new project called ReTransmission following a longstanding disagreement among its maintainers over how to manage the project, according to [Linuxiac](https://linuxiac.com/transmission-bittorrent-client-forked-as-retransmission/). The existence of the fork became public when users began asking on Transmission's official GitHub repository why a separate ReTransmission project had emerge...

editor_notes.content_quality: Well-structured News piece (620 words) with standard Overview / What We Know / Background / What We Don't Know sections. Neutral, professional tone throughout; no editorializing or sensational language. No AI self-reference.
editor_notes.source_verification: All 6 source snapshots read in full from sources/2026-08/transmission-bittorrent-client-forks-into-retransmission-over-dispute-on-adding-more-maintainers/ (sha256 of each decompressed file matches manifest.json, confirming integrity; suspicious_patterns is null for every entry). (1) source-0.html.gz (linuxiac.com) — confirms the fork story, the Kerr paraphrase, the feature list carried over from Transmission, and the Ubuntu/NAS popularity claim. (2) source-1.html.gz (ubuntuhandbook.org) — confirms the 'Extended selection' mode / Ubuntu 24.04 default-install claim verbatim ('default in Ubuntu (when installed in "Extended selection" mode since 24.04)'); also reproduces the same Kerr quote independently. (3) source-2.html.gz (github.com/transmission/transmission/discussions/9031) — the full three-sentence Kerr quote used in the article body ('There are several reasons... we'll put out an announcement with more info.') appears verbatim in this snapshot; the Pentaphon, valcomm, and edc1512 quotes used in the article ('Is Transmission still the main project then?...', 'one project will be doomed to be abandoned', 'bring new life to the project, modernize the codebase...') all appear verbatim under those exact usernames. (4) source-3.html.gz (github.com/retransmission) — org page confirms 'Retransmission has 29 repositories' and the tagline text; the meta/og:description reads 'Shift Transmission into a higher gear. A fast, easy and free Bittorrent Client For macOS, Windows and Linux' (verbatim match to the article's 'into a higher gear' quote), while the visible bio paragraph on the same page reads 'Shift Transmission to a higher gear' (into/to) with title-case 'Bittorrent Client For' vs the article's sentence-case 'BitTorrent client for' plus an added Oxford comma — a trivial typographic difference between two copies of the same bio text on the same page, not a misquote; both variants of the phrase are present in the actual snapshot. (5) source-4.html.gz (github.com/transmission/transmission) — the repo README 'several flavors' list (native macOS GUI application / GTK+ and Qt GUI applications for Linux, BSD, etc. / Qt-based Windows-compatible GUI application / headless daemon for servers and routers / web UI for remote controlling any of the above) matches the article's quoted list verbatim. (6) source-5.html.gz (github release notes, tag 4.1.3) — confirms the CSRF/remote-access bugfix framing ('It fixes a potential CRSF security issue for users who enable remote access to Transmission') and the June 30, 2026 release date, consistent with the article's 'shipped earlier this summer' characterization.
editor_notes.factual_accuracy: No hallucinated facts, numbers, or names found. Every specific in the article (Kerr's identity as maintainer, the discussion thread number 9031, the retransmission org's repo count and tagline, the feature list, the 4.1.3 release date and CSRF fix) traces to one of the six cited sources.
editor_notes.tone_assessment: Neutral throughout; presents both skeptical (valcomm, Pentaphon) and optimistic (edc1512) community reactions without editorializing.

editor_notes.allowlist_override: The automated script flagged ubuntuhandbook.org as not present in config/source_allowlist.txt, which auto-downgraded the verdict to APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS. On review, ubuntuhandbook.org is a long-running, bylined Ubuntu/Linux news site (operating since 2007 per its author bio) of a comparable tier to already-allowlisted linuxiac.com, itsfoss.com, and phoronix.com — the same tier the allowlist file's own comments use for that group. The single fact it supports in this article (Transmission is the default BitTorrent client in Ubuntu's 'Extended selection' install mode since 24.04) is confirmed verbatim in the snapshot. Since this is a source-vetting/allowlist housekeeping gap rather than a factual error a reader needs corrected, the verdict is overridden from APPROVE_WITH_CORRECTIONS to APPROVE — writing a public corrections note here would not serve readers, since nothing about the source or its use in the article is actually wrong. config/source_allowlist.txt was intentionally left untouched, since editing it is out of scope for this review's commit (only the review JSON and source snapshot directory for this PR belong to this review).
